source: Drafted for the macos-arm64-foundation profile on 2026-09-22, updated 2026-09-23, from a Linux workstation: no macOS host executed anything here. Every sha256 below was obtained from the publisher, never guessed. Node, uv, gh and ai-memory come from the publisher's own checksum file or .sha256 sidecar; llama.cpp and Qdrant publish no checksum file for these assets, so each asset's GitHub release `digest` field was read via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag>` and the asset was additionally downloaded to a scratch directory under $TMPDIR and re-hashed with sha256sum (both agreed). The five npm registry tarballs (codex, claude-code, mcporter, context-mode, socraticode) are byte-identical to what `npm view <pkg>@<ver> dist.integrity` reports, cross-checked by downloading each tarball to a scratch directory and independently sha256- and sha512-hashing it; four of the five are also byte-identical to the ones pinned in adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json (socraticode has no linux-x86_64 pins entry: recipes/README.md documents it there as a manual --ignore-scripts recipe rather than a pins-file entry). codex and claude-code each additionally carry a `platform_dependency`: the darwin-arm64 optional dependency npm itself resolves and installs alongside the pinned wrapper tarball, read 2026-09-23 with `npm view <pkg>@<ver> optionalDependencies` for its identity and `npm view <resolved-package>@<resolved-version> dist.tarball`/`dist.integrity` for its url/integrity, each independently re-downloaded and sha256/sha512-hashed to confirm. It is never installed by trusting npm's own automatic resolution of it (unverified) or by reading back npm's install state afterward (measured directly on this project's own host: npm 11.19.0's `--global --prefix` install writes no lockfile anywhere under the prefix and no package.json `_integrity` field, nests a platform-specific optional dependency under the wrapper's own node_modules regardless of --omit=optional/--no-optional/NPM_CONFIG_OMIT=optional, and overwrites a pre-placed nested copy during its own install pass). adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's install_platform_dependency instead fetches and SHA-256 verifies the platform tarball itself with the same fetch() every other pin uses, then OVERWRITES the unverified nested copy npm's own install just fetched at the exact path Node's own require.resolve (scoped to the wrapper's own directory, and matched against the exact expected nested path -- never trusted if it resolves anywhere else, since require.resolve's GLOBAL_FOLDERS fallback can point outside the prefix entirely) finds it from, falling back to a top-level alias only when nothing is nested there at all; it then re-verifies both the resolved path and the resolved package's own name against this pin's `resolved_package` before running `npm rebuild` to trigger any lifecycle script the wrapper's own --ignore-scripts install deferred. Versions match pins-linux-x86_64.json wherever the component is the same.

tools.install_note: Same Node version as the linux-x86_64 pin (24.21.0), different asset. Extract with --strip-components=1 into tools/node-24.21.0; symlink bin/{node,npm,npx,corepack}. Apple Silicon build; no Rosetta.
Same uv version as the linux-x86_64 pin. Archive also contains uvx; install both into tools/uv-0.12.17 and symlink each.

tools.checksum_ref: cli/cli release v2.101.0 asset gh_2.101.0_checksums.txt line 'gh_2.101.0_macOS_arm64.zip', read 2026-09-22
tools.install_note: Same gh version as the linux-x86_64 pin. macOS ships a zip, not a tarball: unzip and take the executable at gh_2.101.0_macOS_arm64/bin/gh. Requires unzip (present in the macOS base system).

tools.checksum_ref: npm view @openai/codex@0.155.1 dist.integrity = sha512-02fAAGyBtlA1zPjEo3kTj/bOSYbPz5DvjLwRZJdV7weFFEDzNFOMjQGmZ/+5CuirYV0hE+AZTrnjzwXYU4AdAQ== (2026-09-22); the tarball was re-downloaded and sha256sum matched adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json exactly
tools.install_note: Platform-independent wrapper package, identical bytes to the linux-x86_64 pin. On Apple Silicon npm additionally resolves the optional dependency '@openai/codex-darwin-arm64', which carries the real binary; see platform_dependency below for its pinned identity. adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's install_npm installs this wrapper with --ignore-scripts (codex has no lifecycle scripts of its own, so that is a no-op for codex specifically, but this pin shares the same code path as claude-code below), then install_platform_dependency fetches and SHA-256 verifies the platform tarball itself and OVERWRITES whatever npm auto-fetched, unverified, wherever Node's own require.resolve actually finds it from inside this wrapper -- measured directly (npm 11.19.0): a plain global install always nests a platform-specific optionalDependency under the wrapper's own node_modules regardless of --omit=optional/--no-optional/NPM_CONFIG_OMIT=optional (none suppressed the on-disk fetch for this no-lockfile install shape) or of pre-placing verified content first (npm overwrote it during its own install pass); only overwriting AFTER npm's own install, at wherever Node itself resolves from, survives.

platform_dependency.name: @openai/codex-darwin-arm64
platform_dependency.checksum_ref: '@openai/codex-darwin-arm64' is not itself a published package: npm view @openai/codex@0.155.1 optionalDependencies (read 2026-09-23) shows it as an npm: alias to '@openai/codex@0.155.1-darwin-arm64', the same package name at a platform-suffixed version. npm view '@openai/codex@0.155.1-darwin-arm64' dist.tarball/dist.integrity read 2026-09-23 gives the url/integrity above; the tarball was independently downloaded to a scratch directory and sha256- and sha512-hashed, both matching (sha512 matches dist.integrity exactly).

tools.checksum_ref: https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/2.1.280/manifest.json (fetched 2026-09-23) lists platforms.darwin-arm64.checksum = 387a5c5dcdbb815085edf0baf79591f9d8894efe922bceaf3d75b1b08055229d; the darwin-arm64 binary itself was independently downloaded (207.2 MiB, matching manifest.size 217254576 bytes reported by the server) and sha256-hashed on this (Linux) host, and the recomputed digest matches the manifest exactly. A manifest.json.sig sidecar exists but this host has no published Anthropic public key or documented verification procedure to check it against, so the manifest's signature itself is UNVERIFIED; treat this pin as byte-verified against the served artifact, not signature-verified. Superseded the prior npm-wrapper + platform_dependency pin (2.1.278, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1): the native installer is now the reference path, matching the linux-x86_64 pin and ~/codex-ecosystem/bin/bootstrap-linux.sh's own claude-code step.
tools.install_note: Fetch the binary, verify its sha256, then run `"$bin" install 2.1.280`, mirroring pins-linux-x86_64.json's claude-code entry (adoption/bootstrap-macos.sh's own *-native case does this). The installed binary self-manages ~/.local/share/claude/versions and the ~/.local/bin/claude launcher and auto-updates on the latest channel from there; this pin is a floor, not a ceiling, and no DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER opt-out is set. This drops the old npm platform_dependency entirely; the native binary needs no nested @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64 package or install.cjs postinstall copy step.

tools.checksum_ref: npm view mcporter@0.13.13 dist.integrity = sha512-rgltHjpmdsBzErnWfAlNsW6Sn5B3y3Qli8phNtKkgn7s/Lk3Uf1YWLpqJXrIXjhxzBR67Oi5Z3+wxptn/vxFkA== (2026-09-22); re-downloaded tarball sha256 matched the linux-x86_64 pin exactly
tools.install_note: UNPINNED DEPENDENCIES: this sha256 covers mcporter's own registry tarball only. `npm view mcporter@0.13.13 dependencies bundleDependencies optionalDependencies` (2026-09-22) lists ten runtime dependencies (@iarna/toml, @modelcontextprotocol/client, @modelcontextprotocol/server, acorn, commander, es-toolkit, jsonc-parser, ora and zod as caret ranges; rolldown exactly 1.2.8) and no bundled or optional ones, so npm resolves those packages from the registry at install time outside this hash; rolldown@1.2.8 in turn selects its native optionalDependency '@rolldown/binding-darwin-arm64@1.2.8' on Apple Silicon. Requires Node >=24, satisfied by the node pin above.

tools.checksum_ref: npm view context-mode@1.0.169 dist.integrity = sha512-94JIaFuLjF9SO2BsGTrbGtyT44K95+9OC8BdbaL/UT76xOkanJLfUR5CzmNw+GELXZQqH4nBrKg9wjBnSFkVnQ== (2026-09-22); re-downloaded tarball sha256 matched the linux-x86_64 pin exactly
tools.install_note: No optionalDependencies on the registry (checked 2026-09-22). As in the linux-x86_64 pin, the npm package is a DIFFERENT source revision from the client-native Context Mode plugin and installing it does not establish plugin-level acceptance.

tools.checksum_ref: akitaonrails/ai-memory release v2.3.2 asset ai-memory-macos-aarch64.tar.gz.sha256, read 2026-09-22
tools.install_note: Same ai-memory version as the linux-x86_64 pin; macos-aarch64 sidecar binary archive. Installs the single ai-memory executable. The MCP server registration, hooks install and any managed run remain separate macOS steps with no receipt yet.

tools.checksum_ref: gh api repos/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tags/b11057 asset digest sha256:443eadead90d44c3925b7163012430b2df4934df881cf72a4d94fc71d1380da1 (size 11178107), and an independent sha256sum of the downloaded asset in a $TMPDIR scratch directory returned the same value on 2026-09-22
tools.install_note: Build b11057 matches the 'b11057 (0.4.1-dev)' llama-cpp row in manifests/stack.json; llama-server is a required_command of the macos-arm64-foundation profile, so it is pinned rather than left to a floating `brew install llama.cpp`. OBSERVED ARCHIVE LAYOUT (tar -tzf on the downloaded asset, 61 entries): one flat top-level directory llama-b11057/ holding every executable (llama-server, llama-cli, ...) NEXT TO its dylibs (libllama*.dylib, libggml*.dylib, libmtmd*.dylib) -- there is no build/bin subdirectory in this macOS asset. The whole directory is therefore installed into tools/llama-cpp-b11057 and bin/llama-server is a wrapper script that exports DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH to that prefix and execs the real binary, not a bare symlink. Metal embedding acceptance (port 8232, 768-dim) is unrun.

tools.checksum_ref: gh api repos/qdrant/qdrant/releases/tags/v1.19.1 asset digest sha256:e060209dfefc9d977ddcec48521349f505f8fd1ce21f2a3db444140870522fe4 (size 27974838), and an independent sha256sum of the downloaded asset in a $TMPDIR scratch directory returned the same value on 2026-09-22
tools.install_note: Version 1.19.1 matches the qdrant row in manifests/stack.json. The archive is a single top-level file named qdrant (tar -tzf shows exactly one entry), so the generic single-binary tarball installer applies. Collections are re-indexed on the new host, never copied.

tools.checksum_ref: npm view socraticode@1.14.0 dist.integrity read 2026-09-23; the tarball was downloaded to a scratch directory and independently sha256- and sha512-hashed, both matching
tools.install_note: Not part of adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json: recipes/README.md documents socraticode 1.14.0 with --ignore-scripts as a manual Linux install recipe rather than a pins-file entry (`npm install --global --prefix "$STACK_HOME/tools/socraticode-1.14.0" --ignore-scripts socraticode@1.14.0`). This pin brings macOS the same reviewed version and --ignore-scripts convention, so socraticode is no longer a documented, unpinned skip on this platform. AGPL-3.0-only; --ignore-scripts (this pin's own ignore_scripts:true field, read by install_npm) skips native postinstall/build steps exactly like the Linux recipe. Only a reviewed archive hash, not a claim of a working native codebase-index handshake on macOS.

models.checksum_ref: Hugging Face tree API lfs.oid for ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-GGUF@0f741b5a6585bd53aeb15cd1372c56f2a0f65e12/embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf, equal to a local sha256sum, read 2026-09-23
models.install_note: Round 3h: the llama-embed launchd agent had no -m flag at all (it would restart in a loop, never serving embeddings). Downloaded and verified by bootstrap-macos.sh's dedicated install_embed_model step (not the generic tools[] dispatch above: this is a single raw GGUF file, never an archive to extract) into $ECO_INSTALL_ROOT/state/models/embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf. The llama-embed template's -m flag names this same path via EMBED_MODEL_PATH (adoption/hosts/<host>.json or --set). Kept in this separate models[] section, not tools[], so it is never swept into adoption/manifest.json profile-component coverage.
